openings.claim: The stipulated opposite-corner lift challenges tighter-is-better fastening. It supports coupled loading, without identifying hatch curvature, seal compliance or pressure distribution as the cause.
openings.delta: Change the pressure carrier from left-corner concentration to two balanced, removable padded strip-clamp pairs: four strips, four bolts and four pads. Keep bolt/nut sets engaged and tether removed clamp assemblies outside the inspection opening.
openings.prediction: Load-distribution hypothesis: balanced placement reduces opposite-corner lift while controlling sliding. Nearest rival: hatch/seal geometry dominates, so lift persists or moves despite balancing. Record differing corner heights and displacement; matching bolt turns cannot establish matching clamp force.
openings.probe: Conditional on accessible rim geometry, compare balanced and left-biased placements using the same assemblies. Allocate one ordinary and one right-card-disturbed rival closure/pull, then ten balanced opening cycles with closure/pull measurements; disturb the final closure. Use ruler/marks, 20 N scale and stopwatch. Record corner lift, position, reopening time and visible seal condition. Remove assemblies fully for inspection. The two rival trials provide screening evidence only; order and prior seal loading confound causal comparison.
assumptions: Rim access and strip span permit reversible clamping without hatch/trough deformation; these dimensions are unprovided.
The cord can retain complete assemblies outside the opening, and one technician can release them within 30 seconds; neither is established.
Fabrication fits ninety minutes and twelve trials fit twenty minutes; feasibility must be checked before using the allocation.

assessment: This is a conditional probe, not deployment or demonstrated performance. Defeat the balanced candidate if ten cycles leave position beyond 1 mm, fail the 20 N pull, exceed 30 seconds reopening, create a visible seal tear, or obstruct inspection. The disturbed closure must meet these requirements; continuous seal contact is exempt there. Persistent lift weakens the distribution account but does not prove the geometry rival. Unknown clamp force, contact placement and unequal trial counts prevent causal attribution. The twelve-trial budget provides ten-cycle evidence for only one configuration.
